title: Strings: Hashing, KMP / Z-function, Trie
relevance: High (pattern matching, tries, and rolling hashes show up constantly in OAs; KMP/Z are the standard upgrade from naive search)
company_notes: Dictionary/autocomplete APIs: Trie insert/search/startsWith, sometimes with '.' wildcards (LC 208 / 211 style — Amazon, Google phone screens). Needle in haystack / period checks: first index of pattern, repeated block, shortest palindrome by prepending — KMP or hashing in timed OAs. Grid word hunt: Word Search II — trie + backtracking. Contest-style CP OAs: overlapping word compression, good-substring counts, max-XOR multiset queries (CF hashing / binary-trie, Div. 2 C/D ideas).

phases.goal: Map wording to rolling hash, KMP/Z matching-borders-periods, dictionary trie, binary-trie XOR, or trie+grid search.

must_hit.point: Signals like find/count pattern occurrences, longest border/period, merge on overlapping prefix-suffix, or distinct substrings under constraints point to hashing and/or KMP/Z.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Lists those string-search/border/period/merge/distinct-substring cues and ties them to hash or π/Z tools.

must_hit.point: Autocomplete / dictionary queries with insert, search, and startsWith (sometimes '.' wildcards) signal a trie, not a flat map scan.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names Trie API shape and optional wildcard DFS (LC 208 / 211 style).

must_hit.point: Maximize XOR with inserts/deletes signals a binary trie, not a sorted-array scan per query.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Says bit-by-bit trie for max XOR under live insert/delete.

must_hit.point: Find all dictionary words on a board (Word Search II) signals trie + grid backtracking as the expected optimal path.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Recognizes board multi-word hunt pruned by a dictionary trie, not one DFS per word alone.

Would you reach for hash, KMP/Z, or a trie here—and why?

hints.1: Listen for pattern find/count, border/period/overlap merge, autocomplete, max XOR with updates, or board dictionary hunt.
hints.2: Occurrences/borders/periods/overlap → hash or KMP/Z; insert/search/startsWith or '.' → trie; max XOR insert/delete → binary trie; board words → trie+DFS.
hints.3: Say: find/count/border/period/prefix-suffix merge/distinct constrained substrings → hashing/KMP/Z; autocomplete insert/search/startsWith (± '.') → trie; max XOR with inserts/deletes → binary trie; Word Search II → trie + backtracking.

phases.goal: State the near-linear string plan: prefix hashes, π/Z matching, trie dictionary, or binary-trie XOR before coding.

must_hit.point: Treat strings as sequences searchable in near-linear time: rolling hash turns any substring into an O(1) fingerprint after prefix-hash precompute (double-hash on CF).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Plans prefix hashes then O(1) substring fingerprints, mentioning double-hash for CF.

must_hit.point: KMP’s π-array / Z-function answer longest prefix that is also a suffix / matches at i, unlocking matching, borders, and periods in O(n).
must_hit.evidence_hint: States π/Z meanings and that they unlock matching, borders, and periods linearly.

must_hit.point: A trie stores a dictionary by shared prefixes for insert/search/startsWith, multi-pattern search, and XOR-maximization via a binary trie.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Plans prefix-sharing trie for dictionary ops and binary trie for max XOR.

must_hit.point: Prefer hash for flexible compares / binary search on length; KMP/Z for exact linear matching with no collision worry; trie when many patterns or prefixes dominate.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Picks among hash vs KMP/Z vs trie with those preference rules.

probes: Walk through how you would search or compare substrings here—hash, KMP/Z, or trie?
When do you prefer rolling hash over KMP/Z, and when is a trie the right structure?

hints.1: Separate fingerprint compares, linear π/Z tools, and prefix-dictionary / XOR tries.
hints.2: Prefix hashes → O(1) substring hash; π/Z → matching/borders/periods; shared-prefix trie or binary XOR trie for dictionary/XOR.
hints.3: Say: rolling hash = prefix hashes + O(1) fingerprint (double-hash on CF); π/Z unlock matching, borders, periods in O(n); trie for insert/search/startsWith / multi-pattern / binary max-XOR; prefer hash for flexible compares/BS on length, KMP/Z for exact linear no-collision, trie for many patterns/prefixes.

phases.goal: Code rolling-hash, π/Z templates, border/period recovery, and trie / binary-trie mechanics from memory.

must_hit.point: Rolling-hash template: prefix hashes, O(1) substring hash, two mods (or 2^61-1), base > |Σ|, map 'a' ↦ 1 (never 0).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Recites prefix hashes, dual mod / 2^61-1, base above alphabet, and non-zero 'a' mapping.

must_hit.point: Write the π-array (KMP failure) and Z-function from memory; convert matching into a single concatenated string with a sentinel.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Sketches π and Z builders and pattern+sentinel+text concatenation for matching.

must_hit.point: Recover all borders by repeatedly jumping π[i]-1; detect periods from Z / borders (i is a period iff i+z[i] ≥ n).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Walks the border chain via π jumps and states the Z period rule.

must_hit.point: Trie node: next[26] / map + isEnd (+ optional cnt); DFS for '.' wildcards; prune Word-Search-style board DFS through the trie.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Codes children array/map, end flag, wildcard branching, and board DFS pruned by trie edges.

must_hit.point: Binary trie for max-XOR with insert/delete and path counts.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Maintains bit-path counts so insert/delete keep max-XOR queries correct.

probes: Write the rolling-hash and π/Z templates you actually use in contests.

hints.1: Start from prefix hashes and the π/Z builders, then borders/periods and trie fields.
hints.2: Hash: two mods or 2^61-1, 'a'→1; matching via sentinel concat; borders = π jumps; periods from Z; trie next[26]+isEnd; binary trie with counts.
hints.3: Spell: prefix hashes + O(1) substring hash, dual mod/2^61-1, base>|Σ|, 'a'↦1; π and Z from memory with sentinel concat; borders via π[i]-1 jumps; period iff i+z[i]≥n; trie next[26]/map+isEnd(+cnt), '.' DFS, board prune; binary trie insert/delete path counts for max XOR.

phases.goal: Confirm O(1) substring hashes after precompute and O(n) KMP/Z matching versus naive quadratic search.

must_hit.point: After prefix-hash precompute, any substring fingerprint is O(1); matching, borders, and periods via π/Z run in O(n).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Separates O(1) hash queries from linear π/Z passes for matching/borders/periods.

must_hit.point: Needle-in-haystack must get past naive O(nm) using KMP, Z, or Rabin–Karp-style hashing.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Rejects nested scan as the intended OA solution and names a linear or hash matcher.

probes: What is the cost of a substring hash after prefix precompute, and of π/Z matching?
Why is naive double-loop search not enough for first-occurrence / string-matching drills?

hints.1: Separate precompute from per-query hash cost, and naive search from linear tools.
hints.2: Prefix hashes → O(1) fingerprint; π/Z → O(n); naive first occurrence is O(nm).
hints.3: Say: O(1) substring hash after prefix hashes; matching/borders/periods in O(n) via π/Z; upgrade from naive O(nm) with KMP, Z, or Rabin–Karp.

phases.goal: Catch zero-mapped alphabet hashes, missing double-hash, broken border/period recovery, and wrong tool choice.

must_hit.point: Mapping 'a' ↦ 0 in a rolling hash collapses leading-a prefixes and breaks substring fingerprints; use 'a' ↦ 1.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Calls out never-zero alphabet mapping as a hard hash template rule.

must_hit.point: Single-mod hashing on CF invites collisions; use two mods (or 2^61-1) when compares must be trusted.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Insists on double-hash or 2^61-1 for contest substring equality.

must_hit.point: Forgetting the sentinel when concatenating pattern and text corrupts π/Z matching across the boundary.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Requires a separator so failure links / Z boxes cannot cross pattern into text spuriously.

must_hit.point: Skipping the π border chain or the Z period test (i+z[i] ≥ n) misses Finding Borders / Finding Periods style answers.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Recovers all borders by π jumps and checks periods with the Z inequality.

probes: What goes wrong if the hash alphabet maps 'a' to 0 or you trust a single mod on CF?
How do you safely run KMP/Z matching and recover every border or period?

hints.1: Check alphabet base mapping, collision policy, sentinel, and border/period recovery.
hints.2: 'a'→1 never 0; double-hash or 2^61-1 on CF; sentinel between pattern and text; walk π for borders; i+z[i]≥n for periods.
hints.3: Say: never map 'a' to 0; double-hash (or 2^61-1) on CF; concatenate with a sentinel; recover borders by jumping π[i]-1; i is a period iff i+z[i]≥n.

tradeoffs.strong_answer: Prefer hash for flexible substring compares and binary search on length; prefer KMP/Z when you need exact linear matching, borders, and periods with no collision worry.

Hash/KMP/Z excel at single-pattern search, borders, periods, and overlap merges; a trie is better when many patterns or shared-prefix dictionary queries (insert/search/startsWith, wildcards, board multi-word hunt) dominate.
A character trie stores words by shared prefixes for autocomplete and multi-pattern board search; a binary trie stores numbers bit-by-bit for max-XOR queries with insert/delete and path counts.

gotchas.trap: Mapping 'a' to 0 in the rolling-hash alphabet.
gotchas.correction: Map 'a' ↦ 1 (never 0); keep base > |Σ|, use two mods or 2^61-1, and precompute prefix hashes for O(1) substring fingerprints.

gotchas.trap: Trusting a single-mod hash for equality on CF.
gotchas.correction: Double-hash (two mods) or use 2^61-1 so substring compares are contest-safe.

gotchas.trap: Running KMP/Z matching on a raw pattern+text concat without a sentinel.
gotchas.correction: Insert a sentinel so π/Z cannot falsely match across the pattern–text boundary.

gotchas.trap: Computing only π[n]-style one border and stopping.
gotchas.correction: Recover all borders by repeatedly jumping π[i]-1; detect periods from Z/borders (period iff i+z[i] ≥ n).

gotchas.trap: Solving Word Search II with per-word board DFS and no dictionary structure.
gotchas.correction: Build a trie over the dictionary and prune board DFS through trie edges (expected optimal path).

gotchas.trap: Answering max-XOR with inserts/deletes via a static sorted list.
gotchas.correction: Maintain a binary trie with insert/delete and path counts so each query walks the opposite bits.
